entry.title: Shfli: a Syrian online marketplace for cars, real estate, auctions, bazaars and jobs
entry.summary: Shfli is an online marketplace for Syria that brings buyers and sellers together in one place: cars, real estate, live auctions, bazaars, jobs and more. Emad Alhamou was its technical lead and co-founder, and built the backend systems behind the platform and the app.
entry.content:
What is Shfli?

Shfli (شفلي in Arabic) is an online marketplace and app for Syria. It connects sellers and buyers in one place, across cars, real estate, live auctions, bazaars and jobs. On its website, Shfli describes itself as the first platform for buying and selling in Syria.

It combines classified ads and e-commerce with live auctions in one interactive marketplace, so buying, selling and finding work all start from the same place.

What you can find on Shfli

Shfli groups its offers into sections: cars, real estate, live auctions, bazaars, jobs, electronics and more. It is an all-in-one platform for buying, selling and auctions, bringing deals and opportunities into one place.

Built for the Syrian market

  • A marketplace with many categories: one platform for different kinds of deals, with live auctions and bazaars alongside the classified listings.
  • Local maps and a tailored experience: maps and routing tuned to the Syrian market, and an experience designed for phones as well as the web.
  • Fast cloud infrastructure and advanced APIs: the cloud infrastructure and the REST APIs were designed for very fast performance and 99.9% uptime.

Who is behind Shfli

Emad Alhamou, the author of this site, was Shfli's technical lead and co-founder. From February 2025 to April 2026 he led the technical team and built the backend systems for the platform and the app.

Frequently asked questions

What is Shfli?

Shfli is an online marketplace and app for Syria. It brings buyers and sellers together in one place, with sections for cars, real estate, live auctions, bazaars, jobs and electronics.

What can I buy and sell on Shfli?

Shfli's sections cover cars, real estate, electronics and more, and it also has live auctions, bazaars and jobs.

Does Shfli have live auctions?

Yes. Live auctions are one of Shfli's sections, next to bazaars and jobs.

Is there a Shfli app?

Yes. Shfli is available as a website and as an app. Start at shfli.com.

Where does Shfli work?

Shfli is built for Syria.

Who built Shfli's technology?

Emad Alhamou, the author of this site, led Shfli's technical team and built its backend systems, as technical lead and co-founder, from February 2025 to April 2026.

entry.title: Arab Solutions: Arabic-first AI customer support that answers from your own knowledge
entry.summary: Arab Solutions is the AI customer support platform our team at Alhamou builds for businesses in the Arab world. It turns a company's documents into an assistant that answers customers in Arabic, shows where each answer comes from, and hands the conversation to a person when it should.
entry.content:
What is Arab Solutions?

Arab Solutions (حلول عربية in Arabic) is an AI customer support platform built Arabic-first. A company adds its documents and knowledge base, and the platform turns them into an assistant that understands customers' questions and gives accurate, consistent answers. You can find it at omysyria.com, under the O My Syria brand.

Our team at Alhamou has been building it since April 2026, for businesses in the Arab world. We pay special attention to Arabic, to privacy and to easy integration with apps and websites.

How the assistant answers

The AI Support Assistant (خدمة المساعد الذكي) is the core of the platform, and it is made to be trusted with customer questions:

  • Answers come from your knowledge: the assistant answers from the documents a company has approved. If the information is not there, it does not guess.
  • Sources you can check: an answer points to the passage and the file it came from, with the date it was last updated and a confidence score.
  • A person when it matters: when a conversation needs a human, the platform hands it to the team with an automatic summary and the reason for the handoff.

Technically this is retrieval-augmented generation (RAG): the platform first finds the relevant parts of your knowledge, and the assistant answers from them.

All your channels in one place

Customers write wherever it suits them, and Arab Solutions brings those channels together:

  • Your website or online shop: a chat widget you add with a single line of JavaScript.
  • WhatsApp Business and Facebook Messenger: the assistant replies in the apps your customers already use.
  • Your own apps: a Messages API that takes a question and returns a grounded answer, with documentation for developers.

Arabic first

Arabic is the starting point, not an add-on. The interface works right-to-left, and the assistant is built to understand Syrian, Levantine, Gulf and Egyptian dialects as well as business Modern Standard Arabic. English is supported too.

Your data stays yours

According to the platform's privacy policy, a company's documents, texts and conversations are not used to train or improve public language models. Data is encrypted in transit and at rest, the data of each organization is kept isolated from the others, and a company can export its records or delete them for good from the dashboard.

A second service: Maps Service

Besides the assistant, O My Syria offers a new Maps Service (خدمة الخرائط) for Syria, through one API: routes with turn-by-turn directions for cars, trucks, bicycles and walking, travel times and distances between many points, place search with autocomplete, reverse geocoding, nearby places and map matching. Active coverage includes Damascus and its countryside, Aleppo, Homs, Hama, Latakia, Tartus and Idlib.

Who is behind Arab Solutions

We are a team of developers at Alhamou (Hamou Software Co.), a software company registered in Damascus, and we build Arab Solutions together. We follow the same rule in everything we make: good technology does not show off its complexity, it makes people's lives simpler.

Frequently asked questions

What is Arab Solutions?

Arab Solutions is an Arabic-first AI customer support platform. A company adds its documents and knowledge base, and an AI assistant answers customers' questions from them, in Arabic and English, on a website or in messaging apps. It is published at omysyria.com under the O My Syria brand.

How does the assistant avoid making things up?

It answers only from the documents a company has approved. Each answer can point to its source passage, with the update date and a confidence score. When the information is missing, the assistant does not answer, and the platform can hand the conversation to a person.

Which channels does it work on?

A chat widget for your website or online shop, WhatsApp Business, Facebook Messenger, and a Messages API for your own apps.

Does it understand Arabic dialects?

Yes. It is built for Arabic and understands Syrian, Levantine, Gulf and Egyptian dialects as well as business Modern Standard Arabic.

Is my company's data used to train AI models?

According to the privacy policy, no. A company's documents, texts and conversations are not used to train or improve public language models, and the company can export or delete its data.

What else does O My Syria offer?

A Maps Service for Syria: routing, place search, geocoding and map matching through one API.

Who builds Arab Solutions?

Alhamou (Hamou Software Co.), a team of developers and a software company registered in Damascus.

Where can I learn more?

Start at omysyria.com and read the developer documentation.

entry.title: TakeCar: a Syrian app for ride sharing between cities, city rides and delivery
entry.summary: TakeCar is the Syrian mobility app our team builds at Alhamou. Drivers fill the empty seats on trips they already make, passengers travel between governorates for less, and the same app covers rides inside the city and delivery.
entry.content:
What is TakeCar?

TakeCar (تيك كار in Arabic) is a mobility app built for Syria. It brings riders and drivers together in one simple experience. Shared rides between governorates are at the heart of the app, and the same app also covers rides inside the city and delivery.

Our team at Alhamou builds TakeCar, and it is our flagship project. We design it for the Syrian market, with a focus on flexibility, ease of use and technology that is owned locally.

How shared rides work

Many drivers travel between Syrian cities anyway, and they often leave with empty seats. With TakeCar, a driver sells the seats of a trip they have already planned at a reduced price instead of travelling empty. Passengers get a shared ride they can rely on, at a good price.

Both sides gain. The driver earns from seats that would have stayed empty, and the passenger travels between governorates for less.

More than intercity trips

TakeCar is not only for long trips. The same app covers rides inside the city and delivery, so one app serves the different ways people and parcels move around.

Built for the Syrian market

  • One experience for riders and drivers: both sides use the same simple app.
  • Flexible pricing and live offers: prices stay flexible, and offers are made live.
  • Maps and routing tuned for the local market: directions that fit the roads and places where the app is used.
  • Infrastructure built to scale: a technical base made to grow with the number of riders and drivers.

Who is behind TakeCar

We are a team of developers at Alhamou, and we build TakeCar together. We follow the same rule in everything we make: good technology does not show off its complexity, it makes people's lives simpler.

Frequently asked questions

What is TakeCar?

TakeCar is a Syrian app for ride sharing and transport. Drivers sell the empty seats of trips they already plan, passengers travel between governorates for less, and the app also covers city rides and delivery.

How does TakeCar make travel cheaper?

A driver who is making a trip anyway sells the empty seats at a reduced price instead of travelling empty. Passengers share the ride, so each of them pays for a seat rather than for a whole car.

Does TakeCar also offer city rides and delivery?

Yes. Besides shared trips between governorates, TakeCar covers rides inside the city and delivery.

Where does TakeCar work?

TakeCar is built for Syria, for trips between governorates and rides inside cities.

Who builds TakeCar?

TakeCar is built by Alhamou, a team of developers, as its flagship project.

Where can I get TakeCar?

Start at takecarapp.com, the official website of the app.

entry.title: Nadhif: clean your Mac with developer tools and protect your website and server from hackers
entry.summary: Nadhif is the Mac app our team is building at Alhamou. It cleans your Mac and explains every file before it touches it, gives developers tools for the gigabytes Xcode, Node and Docker leave behind, and tests your websites and servers for vulnerabilities, so you can close them before anyone uses them.
entry.content:
What is Nadhif?

Nadhif (Arabic for “clean”) is a native macOS app for Macs with Apple silicon running macOS 15 or later. It does three jobs in one quiet window: it cleans your Mac without risk, it clears the space your developer tools quietly fill, and it finds the weak spots in your Mac, your servers and your websites before hackers do.

Our team at Alhamou has been building Nadhif since September 2026, and it is still in active development. The app speaks English, German and Arabic.

Clean your Mac without the fear

Most cleaners ask you to trust one big button. Nadhif works the other way round. A single scan finds caches, logs, developer leftovers, old installers and large files, and every category comes with one line that explains what it is and why removing it is safe, or why it is not. You decide what goes.

Cleaning is a move, not a delete. Everything Nadhif cleans goes to Recently Cleaned, where you can restore it for seven days. Your personal files and your keys are off limits.

The uninstaller removes an app together with its files in Library, and finds what is left of apps you deleted before.

Tools for developers

A developer's Mac fills up in places most cleaners never look. Nadhif knows them: Xcode data, simulators, node_modules folders, Homebrew and Docker, the places that quietly eat gigabytes on a developer's Mac.

Protect your website and server from hackers

The third part of Nadhif looks for the gaps attackers get in through:

  • This Mac: a security check of the Mac you are working on.
  • Servers: scans Debian and Ubuntu servers for vulnerabilities over SSH.
  • Websites: tests the websites you own with real attack techniques, so you find weak spots before someone else does.

Private by design

Nadhif collects no personal data and leaves no process running in the background. Scan results and security reports stay on your Mac.

Who is behind Nadhif

We are a team of developers at Alhamou, and we build Nadhif together. We follow the same rule in everything we make: good technology does not show off its complexity, it makes people's lives simpler.

Frequently asked questions

Is Nadhif safe to use?

Yes. Nadhif explains every category before it cleans, never touches your personal files or keys, and moves everything it cleans to Recently Cleaned for seven days, so you can undo any cleanup.

What do I need to run Nadhif?

A Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15 or later.

Does Nadhif collect my data?

No. Nadhif collects no personal data, and its reports stay on your Mac.

Does Nadhif have tools for developers?

Yes. Nadhif finds and cleans what Xcode, simulators, node_modules folders, Homebrew and Docker leave on your Mac.

Can Nadhif scan my website and server for vulnerabilities?

Yes. Nadhif tests websites you own with real attack techniques and scans Debian and Ubuntu servers for vulnerabilities over SSH.

Where can I get Nadhif?

On the official website, nadhif.hamou.de.
